skill.name: gene-database
skill.description: Query NCBI Gene through E-utilities and Datasets API scripts. Search by gene symbol or ID, fetch metadata, and run batch lookups.
skill.summary: Search, fetch, and batch annotate gene records from NCBI Gene.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: The static alerts are false positives after contextual review. The skill intentionally queries documented NCBI Gene endpoints, uses optional user-supplied NCBI API keys, and contains Markdown examples rather than hidden command execution or prompt injection.

remediation.issue: API keys can be provided on the command line.
remediation.suggestion: Support an environment variable or secure prompt for NCBI API keys, and document the safer option before command-line examples.

remediation.issue: Network requests do not specify explicit timeouts.
remediation.suggestion: Add conservative timeouts to urlopen calls so API outages do not leave workflows hanging indefinitely.

remediation.issue: Batch output writes may overwrite an existing file.
remediation.suggestion: Warn before overwriting output files or add an explicit force option for destructive replacement.

content.value_statement: Gene annotation tasks often require repeated searches across NCBI Gene records. This skill provides scripts and references for symbol lookup, Gene ID retrieval, metadata fetching, and batch annotation.
actual_capabilities: Search NCBI Gene by symbol, name, disease term, pathway, or organism filter.
Fetch Gene IDs and summaries through E-utilities ESearch, ESummary, and EFetch.
Retrieve NCBI Datasets gene metadata by Gene ID, symbol, or taxon.
Process multiple gene IDs or symbols with built-in rate limiting.
Write batch lookup results to a user-selected JSON output file.
Provide reference workflows for disease, pathway, variant, and publication queries.
limitations: Requires internet access to NCBI API endpoints.
NCBI rate limits apply, especially without an API key.
Results depend on current NCBI records and response formats.
Does not interpret clinical significance or provide medical advice.

use_cases.title: Annotate a Gene Panel
use_cases.description: Convert a list of symbols into Gene IDs, descriptions, organisms, chromosome locations, and map locations.

use_cases.title: Check a Candidate Disease Gene
use_cases.description: Search disease-related terms and retrieve summaries for candidate genes in a selected organism.

use_cases.title: Build a Literature-Oriented Gene List
use_cases.description: Use Gene and PubMed link workflows to collect genes connected to publications, pathways, or variants.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Gene ID
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the gene-database skill to find the NCBI Gene ID for BRCA1 in human. Show the command and summarize the expected result.

prompt_templates.title: Fetch Gene Metadata
prompt_templates.scenario: Retrieve readable details for one known Gene ID.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to fetch metadata for Gene ID 672. Include symbol, organism, chromosome, description, and available transcript information.

prompt_templates.title: Batch Annotate Symbols
prompt_templates.scenario: Process a gene list for analysis.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the batch lookup workflow for BRCA1, TP53, EGFR, and KRAS in human. Explain how to save the annotation results to a file.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Pathway Query Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow using search, filtering, and batch retrieval.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a workflow to find human genes involved in MAPK signaling, retrieve summaries, handle rate limits, and document the query parameters.

output_examples.output: The skill returns matching NCBI Gene records, including Gene ID 672, symbol BRCA1, organism Homo sapiens, and chromosome 17.

output_examples.input: Batch lookup BRCA1, TP53, EGFR, and KRAS for human.
output: A batch result list with each query symbol, matched Gene ID, description, organism, chromosome, and map location.
Unmatched symbols are labeled as not found or error instead of being silently omitted.

output_examples.input: Fetch Gene ID 7157 with verbose output.
output_examples.output: The skill displays TP53 metadata, organism details, genomic locations, and a limited list of transcript accessions when available.

best_practices: Always include an organism or taxon when searching by gene symbol.
Use Gene IDs for repeatable workflows after an initial symbol search.
Use an NCBI API key and batching for larger requests while respecting rate limits.
anti_patterns: Do not assume a symbol maps to the same gene across species.
Do not treat NCBI annotations as clinical guidance without expert review.
Do not run large unbatched query loops against NCBI APIs.

faq.question: Which NCBI APIs does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses E-utilities for search and summaries, and the NCBI Datasets API for gene metadata retrieval.

faq.question: Do I need an NCBI API key?
faq.answer: No, but an API key increases the allowed request rate and helps larger batch workflows complete reliably.

faq.question: Can it process multiple genes at once?
faq.answer: Yes. The batch script accepts comma-separated Gene IDs or a file of gene symbols.

faq.question: Can it search non-human organisms?
faq.answer: Yes. The scripts support organism names, common model organisms, and taxon identifiers.

faq.question: Does it download full genome data?
faq.answer: No. It retrieves gene records, summaries, metadata, and related identifiers from NCBI services.

faq.question: Can it replace clinical genetics review?
faq.answer: No. It supports data retrieval and annotation workflows, but clinical interpretation requires qualified review.
